# Resuma

> Resuma is a free, open-source (GPLv3) desktop application for building professional, ATS-friendly resumes. AI is optional: it runs locally on your device by default, you can bring your own model through Ollama, LM Studio, or a cloud API with your own key, or you can choose No AI and use Resuma without any model.

Resuma is a Tauri desktop app (Rust + React) for Windows 10/11, macOS, and Linux, on x64 and ARM64 (Windows on ARM, Apple silicon and Intel Macs, and Linux as an AppImage, .deb, or .rpm). Resumes, settings, and AI models are stored locally and never uploaded or synced. Local AI uses llama.cpp with a Qwen3 model sized for the user's hardware, or any GGUF model downloaded from Hugging Face in the app. With No AI, nothing is downloaded and no AI requests are made; everything except the AI actions keeps working. When AI is on, it can tailor a resume to a job ad: it suggests entries to leave out and new wording for the rest, flags anything a rewording adds, and the user applies, discards, or undoes each suggestion. An optional job-matching model makes this faster with local AI. There are three editor modes: Simple (forms only), Design (colours, section order, and custom sections), and Source (the resume and its template as editable Resuma Markup, `.rsm`). Four templates are built in (Professional, Modern, Compact, and the two-column Sidebar), and users can save their own to a template library. Resumes and settings are encrypted on disk with a recovery key. AI apps that support the Model Context Protocol (MCP) can optionally connect to read resumes and suggest changes the user approves. Resumes export to PDF or plain text, move between devices as `.resume` files, and can be backed up to one password-protected file. The interface is available in English and Serbian.
